Sonia — thanks for the questionnaire, and looping in Neha (Security) and Marcus (Legal) for detail/evidence. Below is a concise response tailored to the hosted API model; attached is a short PDF with the same answers and links to our data-handling playbook.

1) Data residency (hosted API)
- Default: Customer traffic for our public hosted API is served from the region closest to request origin (we operate multi-region endpoints in US-East, US-West, and EU-West). Customer content for the hosted API is stored in the processing region by default.
- EU Data: For customers requiring EU residency we can route and retain data in EU regions; this must be agreed in the account settings or via an enterprise PO.
- Cross-region replication: We do not replicate request/response payloads across regions for the hosted API except for transient replication during active failover operations; long-term backups can be region-specific per account.

2) Default retention windows and options
- Default retention (hosted API): request and response payloads (including prompts, completions, and associated metadata) are retained for 14 days for operational debugging, billing reconciliation, and abuse detection. Usage logs and aggregated telemetry are retained longer for analytics but are pseudonymized.
- Embeddings/Vector Indexing: Customer-managed embedding indexes are retained until explicitly deleted by the customer or by the configured TTL; for hosted ephemeral embeddings we retain snapshots for 30 days by default.
- Opt-out / stricter controls: Enterprise customers can configure 0-day retention (no payload persistence beyond transient memory) or shorter windows via contract; we also support tokenization/partial redaction options where PII is removed before persistence.

3) Deletion / erasure process and SLAs
- Live systems: On receipt of a verified erasure request (API call or support ticket from an authorized admin) we remove the requested data from live stores within 48 hours.
- Backups/snapshots: Backups are immutable for short retention windows; deletion requests will mark the data for purging and it will be removed from regular backups on the next backup rotation. Complete removal from backup snapshots occurs within 90 days in the default configuration. Enterprise customers may negotiate accelerated deletion timelines as part of their contract.
- Evidence: We provide a deletion confirmation report (timestamped events and storage object IDs) upon completion.

4) Backups, snapshots and disaster recovery
- Encrypted backups: Backups are encrypted at rest with customer-mapped keys for Private deployments; for Hosted we manage KMS keys but offer customer-managed keys on Dedicated/Private.
- Retention: Standard backup retention is 90 days. Backups are retained in the same region unless cross-region DR is enabled for the account.

5) Access controls and auditability
- Internal access: Access to customer payloads is strictly limited and audited; access requires break-glass process and is logged for SOC2 reporting.
- Audit logs: We can provide audit trails for access and deletion events as part of evidence packages.

Next steps

- Evidence: Neha, can you attach our SOC2 summary and a short export of the deletion confirmation template? Marcus, please flag any legal caveats.

Sonia — answers inline to your clarifications and next steps below. Neha — adding you for SOC2 and the playbook artifact. Marcus — tagging for any compliance/legal caveats on retention guarantees.

Clarifications:
- Uploaded files vs generated content: Files customers POST to the hosted API (for example PDFs passed for summarization) are treated as request payloads. By default they are retained under the same 14-day retention window unless the account is configured for stricter retention or the customer deletes the object via the API. We recommend customers that need minimal persistence instead use our transient endpoints or enable client-side redaction before upload.
- Recoverability after purge: Objects marked for purge are not accessible via our APIs or internal consoles. Immutable backup snapshots mean physical recovery from backups could be possible until the snapshot retention period expires; we delete objects from subsequent snapshots during normal rotations. For hosted accounts the worst-case window where old objects might be present in immutable snapshots is 90 days.
- Deletion confirmation reports: yes — the standard report includes storage object IDs, timestamps, and an HMAC-signed confirmation token that you can ingest into your audit pipeline.

Artifacts & next steps:
- Neha will attach the SOC2-summary-2027.pdf and a one-page Data Deletion Playbook to the Drive folder you shared.
